en: The Sūtra of the Great Peacock Queen, Mother of Buddhas, Volume One.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān was staying in Śrāvastī, at the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, there was a bhikṣu named Śāriputra who had not long been ordained.
Having recently received full ordination (*upasampadā*), he was studying the Vinaya teachings and was splitting firewood for the community while attending to their bathing needs.

A large black snake emerged from a hole in a rotten tree and bit the big toe of that bhikṣu’s right foot. The venom spread throughout his body; he fell to the ground in a swoon, frothing at the mouth, with his eyes rolled upward.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda, seeing that bhikṣu afflicted by poison and suffering extreme pain, went quickly to where the Buddha was, prostrated at his feet, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
"The bhikṣu Sāti has been bitten by a venomous snake and is suffering great agony, as described above.
Out of your great compassion, O Tathāgata, how shall you rescue and protect him?
Having spoken these words, [he remained silent].
At that time, the Buddha addressed Ānanda:

“I possess the Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī Great Dhāraṇī, which possesses great majestic power; it can extinguish all poisons, fears, calamities, and afflictions, and it gathers in, protects, and nurtures all sentient beings, enabling them to attain peace and happiness.”

"Retain this *dhāraṇī* of mine, the Vidyārājñī Mother of Buddhas, to provide protection for the bhikṣu Śāṇakavāsin; bind the boundary of the earth and bind the boundaries of the cardinal directions, so that he may attain peace and security, and all his suffering and afflictions shall be utterly eliminated."
They may be possessed by devas, nāgas, asuras, marutas, kumbhāṇḍas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, or bhūtas.
Possessed by piśācas, possessed by bhūtas, possessed by kūṣmāṇḍas, possessed by pūtanas, possessed by kaṭapūtanas, possessed by siddhas,
possessed by unmādas, possessed by cetas, possessed by apasmāras, or possessed by u...
When one is possessed or bewitched by Sattaraka or by such others as these, the Vidyārājñī Mother of the Buddha can provide complete protection,
ensuring that there is no sorrow or fear, and that one shall live for a hundred years.
Or if they are subjected to the malevolent rites of others, such as loathsome incantations, sorcery, or the arts of *gū* and *mèi*, namely:

*kṛtyaka*, *karmāra*, *kākhora*, *kīlana*, *vetāla*, or *piśāca*; those who drink the blood and marrow of others, transform people into servants, summon spirits and ghosts, commit various evil deeds, consume foul food or cause foul vomiting, cast evil shadows or evil glares, leap upon or trample over others with malice; or those who create curses through written spells, or perform wicked inversions—should anyone wish to harass or disturb them with such evil acts, this Mother of Buddhas, the Vidyārājñī, shall protect that person along with their retinue, so that none of these evils can cause them harm.

Furthermore, may all malarial fevers—whether occurring every day, every two days, every three days, every four days, or even every seven days, half-month, or month; whether recurring daily or appearing for a mere moment; as well as the four hundred and four diseases, chronic fevers, convulsions, goiters, demonic fevers, disorders of wind, bile, and phlegm, or the "triple-aggregation" (sannipāta) fevers; indigestion; headaches, hemiplegia, pain in the eyes, ears, nose, lips, mouth, cheeks, teeth, and tongue; pain in the throat, chest, ribs, back, heart, belly, hips, abdomen, thighs, and knees; or pain in the limbs, the private parts, or throughout the entire body—may all such afflictions be completely extinguished.

May you protect me, [Name], along with all my retinue; having bound this boundary of the earth and the boundaries of the cardinal directions, by reciting this sutra, may all be rendered peaceful and secure.
He then spoke these verses:
"May I be at peace by night, and at peace during the day; at all times, may the Buddhas protect and keep me in mind."
He then spoke the dhāraṇī, saying: "Tadyathā | iṇi ||"

*Svāhā* (84). "When one who recites this sūtra reaches this point, they must state their specific request according to whatever they seek.
If it is during a great drought, one should say:"
He prays for rain when it is needed;
and when there is excessive flooding, he says:
"May the heavens cease the rain."

Should there be wars, bandits, the spread of epidemics, times of famine and adversity, or any other calamities, if one describes the situation accordingly and makes a request with single-minded devotion, there shall be nothing that is not fulfilled according to one's wishes.
“Ānanda! There are names of nāga kings; you should arouse a mind of loving-kindness and recite their names to neutralize all poisons. They are as follows:
‘I hold the King of Nāgas Dhṛtarāṣṭra in my compassionate thoughts; I always arouse loving-kindness for Varuṇa.’”
Vaiśravaṇa also arouses loving-kindness; I hold Kṛtavarman in loving-kindness.
I have compassion for the Naga King Maṇi; Vasuki the Naga always arouses loving-kindness.
Danda-pāda the Naga King also arouses loving-kindness; Pūrṇabhadra the Naga King I hold in loving-kindness.
To the Nāga Varuṇa of the Anavatapta Lake, to Manasvin and Takṣaka,
and to the Nāgas Nanda and Upananda— I always direct toward them a mind of loving-kindness.
I hold the Naga King Ananta in my compassionate thought; Vāsukī also arouses compassion.
The invincible Naga King always arouses compassion; I hold the Naga King Takṣaka in my compassionate thought.
I hold Mahāmanas in my compassionate thought; Manasvin also arouses compassion.
Aparāntaka and Lokaka, Dhanika, the śrāmaṇera, and the nāga kings;
Nandīmukha and Maṇi, the White Lotus nāga and the Regional Lords;
Karkoṭaka and Śaṅkhapada, Kambala, Aśvajit, and the others—all are compassionate.
Saketa, Kumbhīra, Sūcīloman, and Uragasiras—these nāga kings and others I regard with compassion;
Likhita, I regard you with compassion; Pūrṇa, Karṇa, and Vakra, may I also arouse compassion for you;
Kulika, I regard you with compassion; Vāsuki, Padma, and Sumanas.
The great nāga king Airāvata, and Lambuka, I regard with compassion;
the non-human nāga kings I regard with compassionate mindfulness, and the same applies to the nāga king Uttara;
the nāga king Megha I always arouse compassion for, and the nāga king Mucilinda I regard with compassionate mindfulness.
Some nāga kings travel upon the earth, while some nāga kings always dwell in the sky;
some constantly rely on Mount Sumeru, and some take their abode within the waters.
I hold these one-headed nāga kings in my compassionate thoughts, and likewise those with two heads.
Thus, even unto those with many heads— these dragon kings I hold in loving-kindness;
or again, the classes of footless dragon kings, the two-footed, four-footed, and so forth,
or the various multi-limbed dragon kings— may each give rise to a heart of loving-kindness and protect one another with mindfulness.
These dragon kings possess majestic power; their physical strength and beauty are abundant, and they are renowned.
When the devas and asuras wage war together, they all display great supernormal powers and are valiant.
May footless beings not deceive or despise me; may those with two feet and four feet not harm one another;
and as for the many-footed nāga kings, may they never cause affliction or touch upon my body.
I hold all nāgas and spirits in my compassionate thoughts— those who dwell upon the earth or those who abide in the air—
and may I always cause all sentient beings to give rise to hearts of loving-kindness and protect one another with mindful care.
Furthermore, I pray that all classes of sentient beings, as well as spirits and all great deities,
may always behold every auspicious omen and never witness anything contrary to their hearts or evil and sinful matters.
I constantly give rise to thoughts of great compassion, Causing them to eliminate all evil poisons;
Benefiting and gathering them in so they may leave behind calamities, Constantly providing protection wherever they may be in time and place.
"To all those practitioners of purity who are able to subdue all evil karma—
homage to such as these, who always protect me.
Whenever I encounter various terrors or times of every kind of affliction and disturbance,"
Furthermore, during times of calamity, illness, and strange portents,
or when struck by poison and in times of misfortune,
protect me and my kin; may we be free from disease and live for a hundred years.
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"In the past, on the southern slope of the Snowy Mountains, there dwelt a peacock king named Suvarṇaprabha. Every morning he would constantly recite the Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī Dhāraṇī, and by day he was always secure; every evening he would recite it, and by night he was always secure."
He then spoke the dhāraṇī, saying: "Namo buddhāya, namo dharmāya."

*Svāhā* (36). "Ānanda! That Golden Peacock King, at one time, suddenly forgot to recite this Great Peacock Queen Dhāraṇī of the Buddha-Mother.

Consequently, he went with a great multitude of peacock ladies from forest to forest and from mountain to mountain to play; overcome by lustful attachment and intoxicated by negligence, he entered a mountain cave."
Seeking their prey and watching for an opportunity, the hunters used bird snares to bind the Peacock King.

At the moment he was bound, he recollected his original right mindfulness and recited the Great Peacock Queen Dhāraṇī as before; thus, from his tight bonds, he was naturally liberated, and he and his retinue reached their original dwelling place in safety and peace.
Furthermore, he spoke this vidyārāja-dhāraṇī, saying:
"Namo buddhāya | namo dharmāya |"
Namo saṃghāya, namo subharaṇāya.

*Mantra-luna svāhā.* (57) "Ānanda! This Heart Dhāraṇī of the Great Peacock Queen, the Mother of Buddhas, should be recollected by anyone who wishes to enter a village;
it should also be recollected in the wilderness and on the road."
One should also constantly maintain mindfulness; one should maintain mindfulness even when on a pathless road.

One should maintain mindfulness upon entering a royal palace, when encountering bandits, during times of strife and contention, during calamities of water or fire, when meeting with enemies, when in a great assembly, or when encountering snakes or scorpions.
One should maintain mindfulness when being stung by insects, mindfulness when bitten by venomous creatures, and mindfulness during times of various fears;
one should maintain mindfulness during times of wind, bile, or phlegm disorders, or during the three combined humors;
one should maintain mindfulness whenever each of the four hundred and four diseases arises, and whenever suffering and affliction arrive, one should in every case maintain mindfulness.

Why is this? If there is another person who ought to be sentenced to death but is released by paying a fine; who ought to be fined but is released by a light flogging; who ought to be lightly flogged but is released by being scolded; who ought to be scolded but is released by being reprimanded; who ought to be reprimanded but is released by trembling with fear; and who ought to tremble with fear but is naturally liberated—then all their anxieties and afflictions will completely dissipate.

“Ānanda! This Great Peacock Queen Mantra of the Buddha-Mother was proclaimed by all the Tathāgatas together; you should always receive and uphold it, reciting your own name and requesting their protection:

‘May you accept me, [Name], and remove all fears. In times of suffering from swords, staves, shackles, or fetters, may I be liberated from them all. May I always encounter benefit and never meet with calamity or peril. May I live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.’”

This includes gods and their wives, male and female devas, as well as their parents and all their associates; none of such classes can inflict injury.”

Why is this? Because by constantly upholding the *dhāraṇī* of the Mother of Buddhas Vidyārājñī, those gods, nāgas, spirits, and demons who would cause harm shall return to their own abodes; such beings will not be permitted to enter the assembly.

The former claim that it is a branch of the *ari* tree is an error; there is no such tree as the *ari* in the West.

He then spoke the names of the yakṣas:
"May there be auspiciousness for those with two feet; may there be auspiciousness for those with four feet;
may there be auspiciousness on the road, and may there be auspiciousness upon returning."
May there be auspiciousness in the night, may there be auspiciousness by day;
may there be auspiciousness in all places, and may you not encounter any evils.
May every day be virtuous, and may every lunar mansion be auspicious.
"All Buddhas possess majestic virtue, and all Arhats have severed their outflows;
by these words of truth, may I always be auspicious.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"When reciting this Mahāvidyārāja Sūtra, one should speak these words:

'This Great Peacock Queen of Vidyās was proclaimed by the Buddha; may she, through her spiritual power, constantly protect me, benefit and sustain me, serve as my refuge, and grant me peace and auspiciousness, free from all calamities and afflictions. May swords, staves, poisons, and drugs not cause me harm.'"

Now, according to the Dharma, I bind this boundary of the earth and bind the boundaries of the cardinal and intermediate directions; may all sorrows and afflictions be removed, may one live for a hundred years, and may one pass through a hundred autumns.

"Furthermore, Ānanda! There are great yakṣa kings and various yakṣa generals who dwell on the shores of the great ocean, or on Mount Sumeru and other mountains, or who reside in wildernesses, or dwell by rivers, streams, marshes, ponds, charnel grounds, caves, village lanes, crossroads, gardens, groves, and forests, or who dwell in other places; there are great yakṣas who dwell in the royal capital of Aṇavamadra. May these and all such hosts, through this *Buddhamātṛ Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī Dhāraṇī*, protect me, [Name], together with my retinue, so that we may live for a hundred years."
He then spoke the dhāraṇī, saying:
"Tadyathā | hara haraṇi | sara saraṇi | tarapaṇi | moghaṇi | saṃdhavaṇi | jambhaṇi | svāpyantu | svāhā. Furthermore, Ānanda!

In the eastern direction there is a great Heavenly King named Dhṛtarāṣṭra; he is the lord of the gandharvas, who has an entourage of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of gandharvas, and he guards the eastern quarter. He has sons, grandsons, brothers, military generals, ministers, and various envoys—such are his followers.

May they also, by means of this Great Peacock Queen Mother Dhāraṇī, protect me, [Name], along with all my retinue, to eliminate sorrow and affliction, so that we may live for a hundred years and witness a hundred autumns.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:
"Tadyathā | cukkulu | cukkulu | cukkulu | cukkulu | cukkulu | cukkulu | cukkulu cukkulu | cukkulumī svāhā. Furthermore, Ānanda!

Constantly using the fragrance of precepts to polish and adorn the body, Always wearing the robes of meditative concentration to sustain the person,

“With these great nāga kings as their leaders, together with their kin and retinues, they cause this great earth to sometimes tremble and resound, or emit light, or send down sweet rain to ripen the crops. Having already seen the Tathāgata, they have received the three refuges and accepted the precepts; they have stripped away the fear of the garuḍas, escaped the fear of fiery sand, and avoided the fear of royal conscription. They constantly support the great earth, dwell in great jewel palaces, possess long lifespans, and have great power, wealth, and sovereignty. With immeasurable retinues, they are endowed with supernatural powers, capable of crushing enemies. Possessing great radiance and perfect form and color, their fame pervades everywhere. When the devas and asuras wage war, they provide auxiliary divine power so that the devas may achieve victory.”

May all the sons, grandsons, brothers, generals, ministers, and various messengers of those dragon kings likewise use this Great Peacock Queen Buddha-Mother Dhāraṇī to protect me, [Name], and all my retinue, causing us to be free from sorrow and suffering, and to live for a hundred years.

protect the Buddha’s teachings so that they endure for long, and each of you should diligently practice the World-Honored One’s instruction.
All those disciples who have come here, whether dwelling upon the earth or abiding in the sky,
should always give rise to a heart of compassion for the world of humans, and day and night abide themselves in accordance with the Dharma.
May all worlds be ever peaceful and secure; May boundless merit and wisdom benefit all beings;
May all karmic offenses and afflictions be completely eliminated, And may they depart from all suffering to return to perfect nirvana.
Constantly using incense to anoint and brighten the body, Always wearing the prescribed robes to sustain the person,
Adorned everywhere with the wondrous flowers of Bodhi, One dwells in constant peace and happiness wherever one stays.

The power of the Buddha-mother Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī can eliminate all poisons and cause them to enter the earth, so that I, [Name], and all my retinue may attain peace and security.
"Ānanda! Furthermore, there are all varieties of poisons; you should recite their names, which are as follows:

The Bodhisattva Maitreya also rejoices in and proclaims it.

The Great Brahmā Deva King, Lord of the Sahā World, together with Śakra, Lord of the Devas, the Four Great Heavenly Kings—Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Lord of the Gandharvas; Virūḍhaka, Lord of the Kumbhāṇḍas; Virūpākṣa, Lord of the Nāgas; and Vaiśravaṇa, Lord of the Yakṣas—along with the twenty-eight great yakṣa generals, all rejoice in and proclaim this mantra of the Great Peacock Queen, the Mother of Buddhas.
The great general Caṇḍika, Hārītī with her five hundred sons, and all their retinues also joyfully proclaimed it. Ānanda!
No one is able to transgress this mantra of the Great Peacock Queen, Mother of Buddhas.
Whether they be devas, nāgas, asuras, marutas, garuḍas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, or others, none are able to transgress it.

Whether they be yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, pūtanas, kūṣmāṇḍas, bhūtanās, kaṭapūtanas, skandhas, unmādas, cetas, apasmārakas, uṣṭradharakās, or any other such spirits and deities, none whatsoever shall be able to transgress it.

Furthermore, as for all those who consume evil food— those who consume vital essence, those who consume the fetus, those who consume blood, those who consume flesh, those who consume fat, those who consume marrow, those who consume the raw, those who consume life-force, those who consume sacrificial offerings, those who consume breath, those who consume fragrance, those who consume garlands, those who consume flowers, those who consume fruit, those who consume crops, those who consume fire-sacrifices, those who consume pus, those who consume excrement, those who consume urine, those who consume mucus and saliva, those who consume spittle, those who consume nasal mucus, those who consume leftover food, those who consume vomit, those who consume impure things, and those who consume leaking water— all such evil consumers of food likewise cannot transgress this Great Peacock Queen of Wisdom, the Mother of Buddhas.
Furthermore, various malevolent practices such as sorcery,
bewitchment, curses, and incantations— including *kṛtyā*, *karmāṇa*, *kākhorda*, *cikitsā*, *vaitāna*, *piśāca*, and *bhūta*— are likewise unable to transgress [this power].

Furthermore, those who drink the blood and marrow of others, transform people to drive them into servitude, summon ghosts and spirits, or commit various evil deeds; those who consume foul food or vomit foul matter, cast evil shadows or glare with evil eyes; those who create magical spells of suppression (*yantra*), leap about wickedly or stride across with malice, or perform other such evil acts—even they cannot transgress this Great Peacock King Mother of Buddhas (*Mahāmāyūrī*).

Furthermore, kings, thieves, water, fire, enemy armies, famine, untimely death, earthquakes, predatory beasts, hostile enemies, and evil associates—none of these can transgress [the power of this practice]; they shall all be utterly distanced from them.

Furthermore, regarding various malignant diseases—such as scabies, leprosy, sores, and ringworm; hemorrhoids, fistulas, carbuncles, and abscesses; blackened and rough skin; indigestion; headaches and hemiplegia; pain in the eyes, ears, and nose; pain in the lips, mouth, and cheeks; pain in the teeth and tongue; as well as pain in the throat; pain in the chest, ribs, and back; pain in the heart, abdomen, waist, and hips; as well as pain in the spleen and knees; pain in the hands, feet, four limbs, and private parts; emaciation and wasting diseases; and pervasive bodily aches—all such pains cannot prevail against them, and they shall all be completely eliminated.

Furthermore, all types of malarial fevers—those occurring every day, every two days, every three days, every four days, or even every seven days, half-month, or month; those that occur daily or for a mere moment; chronic fevers; ailments of partial paralysis, goiters, and demonic fevers; disorders of wind, bile, and phlegm; or the "triple-aggregation" diseases and the four hundred and four diseases—all cannot transgress this Great Peacock King Mother of Buddhas.

“Ānanda! Furthermore, regarding malevolent spirits, ghosts, non-humans, and the like; all evil poisons and harms; all inauspicious things; all malignant diseases; all ghosts and spirits, along with their messengers; the terrors of enemies; various poisons; incantations; and all forms of sorcery—none can transgress this Mahāmāyūrī Buddha-Mother Vidyārājñī. One shall always remain far removed from all unwholesome karma, attain great auspiciousness, receive the empowerment of the multitude of sages, and have all one’s aspirations fulfilled.”
"Furthermore, Ānanda!
If there is anyone who merely utters the name of this Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī, she will protect that person themselves as well as others."

Alternatively, one may tie a cord and wear it upon the body; for such a person, a death sentence shall be commuted to a fine, a fine shall be commuted to a light flogging, a light flogging shall be commuted to verbal abuse, and verbal abuse shall naturally be dispensed with—thus all sufferings and difficulties shall completely dissipate.

This person shall also not be harmed by kings, thieves, water, fire, poisons, or weapons; neither humans, devas, ghosts, nor spirits will dare to transgress against them. They shall sleep in peace and awaken in peace, free from all terrors, with their merit and virtue increasing and their lifespan extended.

“Ānanda! With the sole exception of those karmic actions from past lives that are fixed and must inevitably bear their fruit, if one merely reads and recites this sutra, one will certainly obtain its corresponding efficacy. Ānanda!”

If there is a drought, or if there is excessive rain, by reciting this sutra, all the nāgas will rejoice; if the rain has lingered too long, it will clear up, and if there is a severe drought, it will surely rain, causing those who seek it to have their wishes fulfilled according to their desires.

“Ānanda! This Great Peacock Queen Mother of Buddhas, by the mere act of recollecting her, can eliminate fear, enemies, and all calamities; how much more so for those who fully read, recite, receive, and uphold it—they will certainly obtain peace and happiness.”

“Ānanda! This Mahāmayūrī Vidyārājñī, the Mother of Buddhas, is capable of eliminating calamities and pacifying enemies; she acts for the purpose of protecting the fourfold assembly—bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās—so that they may be free from all fears.”

At that time, the Venerable Ānanda, having heard this sutra spoken by the Blessed One, prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and, receiving the Buddha’s holy command, went to where the bhikṣu Śāriputra was. There, he employed this Dharma of the Great Peacock Vidyārājñī to provide protection for that bhikṣu; he bound the boundary of the earth, bound the boundaries of the cardinal and intermediate directions, and through gathering and benefiting [the assembly], he removed their suffering and affliction.

At that time, the bhikṣu Śāriputra’s agonizing pain subsided and his body attained peace; rising from the ground, he went together with the venerable Ānanda to the place where the Buddha was, prostrated at His feet, and stood to one side.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda:

"For this reason, you should universally announce to the fourfold assembly—bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās—as well as to kings, ministers, and the people of the world, exhorting them to single-mindedly receive and uphold this Dharma, to explain it to others, to transcribe its scrolls, and to circulate it wherever it may be. You should cause it to be magnificently adorned, establish altars for it, and make offerings of incense, flowers, food, and drink according to one's means, so that all sentient beings may be freed from all sorrows and afflictions, attain immeasurable merit, always enjoy peace and happiness, and live for a hundred years."

At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished preaching this sutra, humans, devas, yakṣas, and all manner of spirits and demons, having received the Buddha’s command, did not dare to transgress it; they all gave rise to hearts of loving-kindness to protect and uphold those who maintain this sutra.

Then the Venerable Ānanda, along with the great assembly—gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, marutas, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others—hearing what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced, and they faithfully accepted and practiced it.
Devas, asuras, yakṣas, and others who have come to hear the Dharma, should listen with a sincere mind;
protect the Buddha’s teachings so that they endure forever, and each of you should diligently practice the World-Honored One’s instructions.
All you disciples who have come here, whether dwelling upon the earth or abiding in the air,
always give rise to a heart of loving-kindness toward the world of humans, and day and night let your own bodies abide in accordance with the Dharma.
May all worlds be ever peaceful and secure; May boundless merit and wisdom benefit all beings.
May all karmic offenses and obscurations be eliminated, And may they distance themselves from all suffering to return to perfect nirvana.
Constantly using the fragrance of precepts to polish and adorn the body, Always wearing the robes of meditative concentration to sustain the person,
Universally adorned with the wondrous flowers of Bodhi, One shall always dwell in peace and happiness wherever one stays.
